brief.subject: IRS sets 2027 brackets; PTINs expire Dec. 31
brief.headline: IRS Releases 2027 Inflation Adjustments as PTIN Renewal Season Opens
brief.dek: New 2027 tax figures, a year-end PTIN deadline, a penalty-relief request for estates and trusts, and state ballot results on taxes.
brief.lede: The IRS has published tax year 2027 inflation adjustments covering nearly 70 provisions, including tax brackets and the standard deduction.

sections.heading: 2027 tax numbers are out
bullets: The IRS updated nearly 70 tax provisions for tax year 2027 to account for inflation.
Brackets and the standard deduction both shift, so owners should revisit withholding and estimated payment plans.
Bookkeepers can start building the 2027 figures into client planning now.

sections.heading: Preparers: renew your PTIN
bullets: Current preparer tax identification numbers expire on Dec. 31, 2026.
Anyone paid to prepare returns needs a valid PTIN, and it must be renewed every year.
Renewing early avoids a gap heading into filing season.

sections.heading: Penalty relief sought for estates, trusts
bullets: The AICPA wants the IRS to waive 2026 estimated tax penalties for certain estates and trusts.
The group flags open questions on how a provision fits with the rules specific to estates and trusts.
Fiduciaries should watch for IRS guidance before making final 2026 payment decisions.

sections.heading: Voters reshape state taxes
bullets: Washington's income tax on high earners survives after backers of repeal measure Initiative 645 conceded.
Colorado supporters claim victory for Amendment 87, which would raise income taxes on high earners.
Florida voters approved cutting property taxes, leaving local governments weighing which services to trim.

brief.seo_description: IRS releases 2027 inflation adjustments, PTINs expire Dec. 31, 2026, AICPA seeks estate and trust penalty relief, plus state tax ballot results.

items.title: AICPA Calls on IRS to Waive 2026 Estimated Tax Penalties for Certain Estates and Trusts
items.snippet: Questions remain about how the provision interacts with the tax rules that specifically govern estates and trusts.

items.title: ‘We’re Going to Be Underwater’: What Florida’s Property Tax Cut Means for Flooding
items.snippet: Florida voters resoundingly decided to slash their own property taxes on election day, sending shockwaves through the local governments who now have to figure out which services to cut.

items.title: Supporters of Colorado’s Amendment 87 Declare Victory for Major Rewrite of State’s Tax Code
items.snippet: Measure would raise income taxes on high earners in seismic change to state fiscal policy.

items.title: Washington ‘Millionaires Tax’ is Upheld as Initiative 645 Fails
items.snippet: Washington's high-earners income tax has withstood an effort to repeal it, as backers of Initiative 645 conceded defeat.

items.title: CPE Webinar: 6 Technology Tips to Save Your Sanity This Busy Season
items.snippet: This webinar examines six automation and workflow technologies that reduce manual processes, standardize operations, and increase capacity. Participants will learn how advanced data extraction, workpaper automation, verification tools, and client collaboration features integrate throughout the tax return preparation cycle to improve overall efficiency and consistency.

items.title: IRS Adjusts Tax Brackets, Standard Deduction for Tax Year 2027
items.snippet: The IRS has released the tax year 2027 annual inflation adjustments for nearly 70 tax provisions.

items.title: Treasury, IRS Designate Over 6,500 Communities as Opportunity Zones
items.snippet: More than 6,500 communities covering all 50 states, the District of Columbia, and five U.S. territories have been federally designated as opportunity zones, the Treasury Department and the IRS announced on Thursday.

items.title: Attention Tax Pros: It’s PTIN Renewal Time
items.snippet: Tax professionals who prepare tax returns must have a valid preparer tax identification number, which must be renewed each year. Current PTINs expire on Dec. 31, 2026.

items.title: ‘AI is Being Overlooked by Small Businesses,’ Says ‘Shark Tank’ Star Daymond John
items.snippet: John took the stage at the LevelUp entrepreneurship conference at the Hilton Anatole in Dallas on Thursday to speak to small business owners about how they can use artificial intelligence to help grow their businesses.

items.title: Proposed Rule: Guidance on Eligible Investments for Trump Accounts; Hearing
items.snippet: This document provides a notice of proposed rulemaking (CC- 00349938-26) published in the Federal Register on August 21, 2026. The proposed regulations provided guidance regarding eligible investments, which are the only assets in which the Trump account may be invested before the first day of the calendar year in which the account beneficiary attains 18.
